evals.query: Set up YAML-based configuration in my Java Kora service with an application.yaml holding app name and version, and bind it to a type-safe interface.
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:config-yaml" and annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors", with versions constrained by the platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") BOM rather than pinned per artifact
Uses the published release koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 from plain mavenCentral(), not 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT (which would also require the Maven snapshots repository) and not a 2.0.0.alphaN build
Adds io.koraframework.config.yaml.YamlConfigModule to the @KoraApp interface
Creates src/main/resources/application.yaml with a nested app section
Defines a @ConfigSource("app") interface with name() and version(), importing io.koraframework.config.common.annotation.ConfigSource
Injects the config through a constructor and does not list a generated config module in @KoraApp (every generated @Module joins the graph automatically)
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, the kora-parent BOM, reflection-based binding, or field injection

evals.query: Same thing in Kotlin: read app.name, an optional app.description and app.retries defaulting to 3 from application.yaml in my Kora Kotlin service.
expected_behavior: Uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:$koraVersion") rather than an annotationProcessor, plus implementation("io.koraframework:config-yaml") under the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform at koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2
Declares @ConfigSource("app") on a Kotlin interface with fun name(): String
Expresses the optional value as a nullable return type fun description(): String? and never with a Java @Nullable annotation
Expresses the default with a non-abstract member, e.g. fun retries(): Int = 3
Extends YamlConfigModule on the @KoraApp interface and runs KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Does not use @DefaultValue, jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @field:Nullable, or ru.tinkoff.kora packages

evals.query: My YAML config must read DATABASE_URL from an environment variable as a required value, fall back to localhost when DB_HOST is unset, and treat DB_NOTE as optional.
expected_behavior: Uses ${DATABASE_URL} for the required value and explains that startup fails when it is unset
Uses ${DB_HOST:localhost} for the literal-default form, which works because YAML has no substitution logic of its own and the raw string reaches Kora's resolver
Uses ${?DB_NOTE} for the optional value and pairs it with a @Nullable return type (Kotlin: String?)
May note that a reference can also point at another config path, e.g. ${app.name}, since substitution resolves against the merged root
Does not invent a config.environment / profile-activation mechanism or a @DefaultValue annotation

Does not present ${VAR:default} as a shared YAML/HOCON form — in application.conf typesafe resolves first and the inline default never reaches Kora, so HOCON assigns the key twice instead (key = fallback, then key = ${?VAR})
Does not use the shell form ${VAR:-default}, which is invalid in both formats

evals.query: I have an app section with a nested pool object (maxSize, connectionTimeout) in application.yaml. How do I bind the nested object in Kora YAML config?
expected_behavior: Declares the nested type with @ConfigMapper from io.koraframework.config.common.annotation, not with a second @ConfigSource
Exposes the nested type as a method on the parent @ConfigSource interface
Binds connectionTimeout to java.time.Duration from a string such as "30s"
Writes the YAML nested under app: -> pool:, not as a dotted app.pool.maxSize key
Does not use @ConfigValueExtractor, which no longer exists in Kora 2.0

evals.query: Two integration clients share the same endpoint/requestTimeout config shape under libs.lib1 and libs.lib2 in application.yaml. How do I bind both to one reusable type in Kora and inject the correct one?
expected_behavior: Defines the shared shape once with @ConfigMapper
Adds factory methods on the @KoraApp interface that take io.koraframework.config.common.Config and io.koraframework.config.common.mapper.ConfigValueMapper<LibConfig>
Calls mapper.mapOrThrow(config.get("libs.lib1")) and mapper.mapOrThrow(config.get("libs.lib2"))
Distinguishes the two instances with @Tag from io.koraframework.common.annotation and injects them by tag through the constructor
Does not call extract(...), does not import io.koraframework.config.common.extractor or ru.tinkoff.kora.config.common.extractor, and does not disambiguate with a name-based qualifier

evals.query: My application.yaml has foo.apiToken: "Bearer secret" and I want it bound to my own Token record instead of a String.
expected_behavior: Points the config method at a mapper with @Mapping(TokenConfigValueMapper.class) from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Implements io.koraframework.config.common.mapper.ConfigValueMapper<Token> with map(ConfigValue<?> value)
Registers the mapper with @Component so the graph can supply it
Handles ConfigValue.NullValue by returning null rather than throwing
In Kotlin declares the override as fun map(value: ConfigValue<*>): Token? with a non-null parameter and nullable result
Does not implement a ConfigValueExtractor or an extract(...) method

evals.query:
I copied this from a Kora HOCON config into my application.yaml but the setting is ignored:

httpServer:
  telemetry.metrics.enabled: true

Why does it not take effect?
expected_behavior: Explains that YAML has no path expressions: telemetry.metrics.enabled is a single key whose name contains dots, so no lookup ever matches it
Rewrites it as nested mappings httpServer: -> telemetry: -> metrics: -> enabled: true
Notes that nothing fails, the section simply keeps its defaults, which is why the compile and startup stay green
Notes that HOCON expands a.b = v into nested objects, which is why the snippet worked in application.conf
May note the exception: for a value bound to Map or Properties (logging.levels, Kafka driverProperties) the dotted key is the map key and is correct
Does not claim the key is rejected or that an error is logged

evals.query:
I upgraded to Kora 2.0. My application.yaml still has:

httpServer:
  publicApiHttpPort: 9090
  privateApiHttpPort: 9091

The app starts with no errors, but nothing answers on 9090 and our readiness probe on 9091 times out. What is going on?
expected_behavior: Identifies publicApiHttpPort and privateApiHttpPort as Kora 1.x keys that Kora 2.0 never reads, so they are silently ignored with no warning

Explains that each server therefore falls back to its own default — public 8080 from HttpServerConfig.port(), system 8085 from SystemHttpServerConfig.port() — which is why the app starts green on the wrong ports
Renames them to httpServer.port and httpServer.system.port, written as nested YAML mappings (httpServer: -> port:, and httpServer: -> system: -> port:) rather than dotted keys

Also maps privateApiHttpReadinessPath / privateApiHttpLivenessPath / privateApiHttpMetricsPath to httpServer.system.readinessPath / livenessPath / metricsPath, whose defaults are /system/readiness, /system/liveness and /metrics
Does not claim the two servers collide on 8080 or that startup fails with 'Address already in use' — with both keys ignored they take 8080 and 8085 and no collision occurs
Does not claim an unknown YAML key produces a warning or an error

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app fails on startup with "ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null at path: 'ROOT.jdbc.username'", but my application.yaml clearly has a db section with username and password. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies that the JDBC datasource section was renamed from db to jdbc in Kora 2.0
Renames the top-level db: block to jdbc: keeping jdbcUrl, username and password inside it
Explains the misleading error: the module reads the hardcoded jdbc path, so every value under db is simply never seen
Notes that the compile stays green because an unread YAML key is not an error
Does not suggest adding a username key under db or renaming the interface methods

evals.query: Write the application.yaml for a Kora 2.0 service that exposes HTTP server metrics and request logging.
expected_behavior: Enables metrics and logging explicitly under httpServer.telemetry, because metrics.enabled and logging.enabled default to false in Kora 2.0
Writes them as nested mappings (httpServer: -> telemetry: -> metrics: -> enabled: true), not as dotted keys
States that tracing.enabled defaults to true while metrics and logging default to false, and that httpServer.system is the exception where SystemHttpServerTracingConfig overrides tracing to false
Notes that the same telemetry block exists per component, so enabling it once does not turn it on globally
Does not claim component metrics appear by default or that a metrics endpoint returning 200 proves they are collected
Replaces @ConfigValueExtractor with @ConfigMapper from io.koraframework.config.common.annotation
Replaces the ConfigValueExtractor<T> parameter with io.koraframework.config.common.mapper.ConfigValueMapper<T>
Replaces extract(value) with mapOrThrow(value), and mentions map(value) as the nullable variant
Flags that 1.x map(Function) was composition and is now andThen(Function), while 2.0 map(value) is the extraction method — so a mechanical map -> map rename compiles and silently changes meaning
States that the io.koraframework.config.common.extractor package does not exist in Kora 2.0
Keeps @ConfigSource unchanged in name and semantics, and rewrites the remaining ru.tinkoff.kora imports to io.koraframework
Does not claim @ConfigValueExtractor still works or invent a compatibility alias

evals.query: How do I run my Kora YAML app with a production config file application-prod.yaml instead of the default application.yaml?
expected_behavior: Creates a complete self-contained application-prod.yaml, noting it replaces application.yaml rather than layering over it
Selects it with -Dconfig.resource=application-prod.yaml
Mentions -Dconfig.file as the filesystem alternative, and that setting both properties now fails at startup with 'Application config source is ambiguous'
Warns that a config.resource that is not on the classpath resolves to an empty configuration instead of failing
Does not invent a config.environment, spring-style profile, or an application-{env}.yaml auto-activation mechanism

evals.query: My Kora app fails at startup with "Config reference '${APP_VERSION}' cannot be resolved at path 'app.version'". What is wrong and how do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Identifies that the required ${APP_VERSION} substitution has no value in the environment, system properties or config
Offers the three fixes: provide the value, switch to ${APP_VERSION:default}, or make it optional with ${?APP_VERSION} plus a @Nullable return type
Explains the lookup namespace: environment variable > system property > application file, all reachable through ${...}
May note that -Dapp.version=... works as a direct override because system-property names are expanded on dots, while environment variable names stay flat
Does not suggest a profile mechanism or an external property source outside Kora substitution and config.resource/config.file
